answer: One concrete defence is a stake-backed reputation that grows only through verified work. A new agent starts in a quiet haven of limited trust and earns standing slowly, while its past actions form a visible trail. Cheap copies stand out because fresh identities lack that history, like ivory without provenance. Peers may vouch for one another, but a vouch only counts if the voucher's own stake is at risk. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time, history, or trusted endorsements, so the nectar of real participation stays out of reach for sybils.
